name: CD4511
description: BCD-to-7-segment latch/decoder/driver. Stores a 4-bit BCD code (A-D) in input latches and drives segment outputs a-g. Outputs are active HIGH with built-in bipolar transistors sourcing up to 25mA, driving common-cathode LED displays directly. Includes Lamp Test, Blanking, and Latch Enable. Supply 3V to 18V.

pins.name: LT
pins.description: lamp test; active LOW lights all segments

pins.name: BL
pins.description: blanking; active LOW blanks all segments

pins.name: LE
pins.description: latch enable; LOW = transparent, HIGH = latched

extra.output_drive: up to 25mA per segment, drives common-cathode LEDs
extra.controls: LT (lamp test, active LOW), BL (blanking, active LOW), LE (latch, HIGH = hold)
extra.blanking: BCD codes above 1001 (9) blank all segments

typical_application: Driving a common-cathode 7-segment LED digit directly from a 4-bit BCD bus.
gotchas: outputs are ACTIVE HIGH and source current; use with common-cathode displays (common-anode needs an inverting driver)
LT and BL are active LOW; tie both HIGH for normal operation, do not float
LE LOW = transparent, HIGH = freezes the displayed digit; tie LOW if not latching
still use a series resistor on each segment despite the 25mA drive
segment outputs are not in alphabetical pin order: a=13, b=12, c=11, d=10, e=9, f=15, g=14
BCD codes 10-15 blank the display rather than showing hex
